text:
Waiting is worse than being born,

because only the one who dies

of waiting without making of life

anything but waiting waits. Waiting for you.


And tied to that waiting of yours that wears me down

and wears down your life without bringing you,

here I am dying of anxieties

because this hope fits here, tremendous.


Each day, oh you who are delayed!

without knowing that we are moving farther away,

the irreparable distance is smaller,

of thinking, of waiting, that may distance us.


And here I go on waiting, I attempt nothing

to flee the torment of your waiting.

I no longer know whether outside my life

others remain or not, whether anyone walking remains!


only for you, for when you arrive,

alone, waiting for you, I wait.

translation.title: Waiting Is Worse Than Being Born...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Conde's obsessive turns on esperar: waiting, waiting for you, and being consumed by waiting.
